featured_reviews.name: Riddhi Purohit
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a very concerning experience at this petrol pump. The staff member did not show me the zero reading before starting the fuel. When I looked at the meter, it already showed ₹300, and there was no usual sound when the fuel began flowing.

When I questioned the attendant, he replied dismissively saying, “Do you think we would do that? You’re a regular here.”
For clarity — I’ve only visited this pump twice. It felt like he assumed that because I was a lady driver and on the phone, I wouldn’t notice.

This incident really shook my trust. I want to warn fellow customers to always check the zero reading and stay alert during refuelling. Transparency and honesty should come first in such places.

Sharing this so others don’t face a similar experience.

People helped me push my car and I took it to side.

Now the only way was to refill the oil and reach my home, but where do I get oil at this time ?

I looked online on Google Maps to check petrol pumps which are near.

After going throughout a list of 'closed' ones. I found this one saying open till 1am.

I called the number. He told me he was open till 1am and he had oil. I explained my situation and he went out of the way and send a person with the oil cans near my location.

So, I really recommend this outlet and thank the owner for the help and trust.

BTW I was with my wife. So you can understand my situation. When I was stuck.

Thank you.

Finding the "best" CNG pump often depends on what you prioritize, as quality can vary by location.
In general, when looking for the best CNG pump, you should focus on:
1. Gas Quality and Pressure
* Pressure (High Fill): A good pump should deliver high pressure (ideally close to or over 200 bar) to ensure your tank is filled completely, giving you maximum range. Low pressure means you get less gas and lower mileage.
* Source/Branding: Pumps run by major and reputable gas distributors or oil marketing companies (like Indian Oil, HP, Bharat Petroleum, Mahanagar Gas, etc.) are generally more reliable in terms of gas quality and accurate metering.
2. Service and Efficiency
* Waiting Time: Due to high demand, quick service is a major plus. Look for pumps with multiple dispensing units or dedicated lines for different vehicle types (e.g., separate lines for cars and autos/commercial vehicles) to reduce wait times.
* Staff Behavior: Courteous and knowledgeable staff contribute to a better experience. They should be able to assist if you have any questions.
3. Reliability and Features
* 24-Hour Availability: For convenience, a 24-hour operational pump is often considered "best," especially for long-distance drivers.
* Payment Options: Pumps that accept various digital payments (UPI, cards) in addition to cash are more convenient.
* Amenities: Features like clean restrooms, a small convenience store, or an air/water station can add to a positive review.
🔎 How to Find the Best-Rated Pump Near You
Since "best" is highly location-specific, the most effective way to find a top-rated one is by using local reviews:
* Map Applications (Google Maps/Apple Maps): Search for "CNG pump" or "CNG station near me." Look for stations with a 4-star rating or higher and read the recent reviews. Users often specifically mention fill pressure, speed of service, and queue length.
* CNG Locator Apps (e.g., Nawgati - CNG Eco Connect): There are apps specifically designed to help you locate CNG stations, check prices, and sometimes see user-reported data on waiting times.
* Local Forums/Groups: Check online car owner forums or local social media groups (like on Facebook or WhatsApp) for your city/route, as users frequently share tips about high-pressure and low-wait-time pumps.

featured_reviews.review_text: I redeemed my IOCL voucher at this pump. The attendant very cleverly asked me before hand about the amount and kept me busy stating that the voucher cannot be redeemed at this pump. Till then the put my voucher amount at the machine and filled petrol in one bike. After that the remaining amount was filled in my car. When I argued that the counter was not 0 before filling, he started giving me vague reasons that it cannot happen like that and the exact voucher amount of petrol will only be filled. After calculating from my car I came to know that approximately rs.400 worth of less petrol was filled in my car. Worst experience ever. I hope it is looked into. Thanks

For sure we will not visit this pump in future.

featured_reviews.review_text: It’s a blatant scam! It’s happened with us more than once now at this pump. Our car will not show even a single km rise in the fuel tank indicator.
